headline: Indian equity markets close September on a weak note amid elevated crude oil prices and persistent FII outflows

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Persistent foreign institutional investor (FII) outflows weighed heavily on market sentiment.
Rising crude oil prices sparked inflationary concerns among investors.
Global rate hikes and international macroeconomic headwinds triggered market outflows.
Intraday volatility led benchmark indices to fail to sustain early trading gains.
whatHappening: BSE Sensex closed around 50 points lower while NSE Nifty logged losses for the third straight day.
Indian benchmark shares logged their worst monthly performance since March.
Sensex and Nifty are set to post their worst nine-month performance in 15 years.
Geojit Financial Services reshuffled its top leadership, appointing Jones George as Managing Director.
summary: Indian benchmark indices closed September on a weak note, with the Sensex and Nifty sliding for a third consecutive session. High crude oil prices, FII selling, and global rate hike worries drove the downturn, marking the worst monthly performance since March. On the corporate front, Geojit Financial Services reshuffled its executive deck while Wipro drew attention regarding long-term investment performance.
